title: Plotting Tools
text:
This chapter introduces various tools and libraries available in R for creating visualizations. It covers base R plotting functions, as well as popular packages like ggplot2 and lattice, which offer advanced capabilities for creating complex and customizable plots.


R’s built-in plotting functions provide a solid foundation for data visualization:


# Scatter plot
plot(x = mtcars$wt, y = mtcars$mpg,
     xlab = "Weight", ylab = "Miles per Gallon",
     main = "Scatter Plot Example")

# Line plot
plot(x = 1:10, y = (1:10)^2, type = "l",
     xlab = "X", ylab = "Y^2")

# Bar plot
barplot(height = c(10, 15, 8, 12),
        names.arg = c("A", "B", "C", "D"))

# Histogram
hist(mtcars$mpg, breaks = 10,
     xlab = "Miles per Gallon",
     main = "Histogram of MPG")



# Multiple plots in one window
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))  # 2x2 grid

plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
hist(mtcars$mpg)
boxplot(mtcars$mpg ~ mtcars$cyl)
plot(density(mtcars$mpg))

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))  # Reset to single plot




ggplot2 is the most popular R package for data visualization, based on the Grammar of Graphics:


library(ggplot2)

# Basic scatter plot
ggplot(data = mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point()

# Adding aesthetics
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "MPG vs Weight by Cylinders",
       x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
       y = "Miles per Gallon")



# Points, lines, bars
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg))

p + geom_point()           # Scatter plot
p + geom_smooth()          # Smooth line
p + geom_line()            # Line plot
p + geom_bar(stat = "identity")  # Bar plot
p + geom_histogram()       # Histogram
p + geom_boxplot()         # Box plot



# Faceting
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ cyl) +
  theme_minimal()

# Custom themes
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw() +
  ggtitle("Custom Theme Example")




Lattice provides trellis graphics for multivariate data:
library(lattice)

# Scatter plot matrix
splom(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])

# Conditional plots
xyplot(mpg ~ wt | factor(cyl), data = mtcars,
       layout = c(3, 1))

# 3D plots
cloud(mpg ~ wt * hp, data = mtcars)





library(plotly)

# Convert ggplot to interactive
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
ggplotly(p)

# Native plotly
plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, type = "scatter", mode = "markers")



library(ggvis)

# Interactive ggplot2-like syntax
mtcars %>%
  ggvis(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg) %>%
  layer_points() %>%
  add_tooltip(function(df) paste("Weight:", df$wt, "MPG:", df$mpg))






library(ggstatsplot)

# Statistical plots with tests
ggbetweenstats(data = mtcars, x = cyl, y = mpg)



library(ggplot2)
library(maps)

# Basic map
world <- map_data("world")
ggplot(world, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "lightblue", color = "black")



library(igraph)
library(ggraph)

# Create network
g <- make_ring(10)
ggraph(g, layout = "circle") +
  geom_edge_link() +
  geom_node_point(size = 5)





Base R: Quick plots, statistical graphics
ggplot2: Publication-quality static plots, complex customizations
Lattice: Multivariate data, trellis displays
plotly/ggvis: Interactive web-based visualizations
Specialized packages: Domain-specific visualizations (maps, networks, etc.)





Know your data: Choose plot types that best represent your data
Keep it simple: Avoid clutter, focus on the message
Use color effectively: Consider colorblind-friendly palettes
Label clearly: Include informative titles, axis labels, legends
Test different tools: Experiment with different packages for the best result

title: Debugging Plots
text:
Debugging plots are essential tools for diagnosing issues in data visualization and analysis. They help identify problems such as incorrect data representation, scaling issues, or unexpected patterns in the data. In this guide, we will explore various techniques and tools for creating effective debugging plots.





Missing or incorrect data types
# Check data types
str(mtcars)

# Check for missing values
sum(is.na(mtcars))

# Visualize missing patterns
library(naniar)
vis_miss(mtcars)
Outliers affecting scales
# Check for outliers
boxplot(mtcars$mpg)

# Use robust statistics
library(robustbase)
summary(mtcars$mpg)





Mapping vs Setting Aesthetics
# Correct: Map color to variable
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point()

# Incorrect: Setting color globally
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(color = "red")  # This sets all points to red
Factor Level Issues
# Check factor levels
levels(mtcars$cyl)

# Reorder factors if needed
mtcars$cyl <- factor(mtcars$cyl, levels = c("4", "6", "8"))
Geom Conflicts
# Error: Can't use geom_bar with y aesthetic
# ggplot(data, aes(x = category, y = value)) + geom_bar()

# Correct: Use stat = "identity"
ggplot(data, aes(x = category, y = value)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity")







# Check ggplot object structure
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
str(p)

# View plot data
p$data
p$mapping



# Build plot incrementally
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg))
print(p1)  # Should show empty plot

p2 <- p1 + geom_point()
print(p2)  # Check if points appear

p3 <- p2 + theme_minimal()
print(p3)  # Check theme application



# Enable ggplot2 debugging
options(ggplot2.debug = TRUE)

# Check for warnings
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()






# Problem: Length mismatch
# ggplot(data, aes(x = x_var, y = y_var, color = short_vector))

# Solution: Ensure vectors are same length or use single values
ggplot(data, aes(x = x_var, y = y_var, color = factor(category)))



# Problem: Wrong scale type
# ggplot(data, aes(x = factor_var, y = numeric_var)) + scale_x_continuous()

# Solution: Use appropriate scale
ggplot(data, aes(x = factor_var, y = numeric_var)) + scale_x_discrete()



# Problem: Typo in parameter name
# geom_point(size = 3)  # Correct
# geom_point(siz = 3)   # Incorrect

# Solution: Check documentation
?geom_point






# Residual plots for model diagnostics
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
plot(model)

# QQ plots for normality
qqnorm(mtcars$mpg)
qqline(mtcars$mpg)



# Correlation plots
library(corrplot)
corrplot(cor(mtcars))

# Pairs plots
pairs(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])



# Plot data distributions
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) + 
  geom_histogram() + 
  facet_wrap(~ cyl)

# Check for data issues
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_text(aes(label = rownames(mtcars)), check_overlap = TRUE)






# When plot fails
tryCatch({
  ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
}, error = function(e) {
  print(e)
  traceback()
})



library(profvis)

# Profile plotting code
profvis({
  p <- ggplot(large_dataset, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point()
  print(p)
})



# Check memory usage
gc()

# For large datasets, use sampling
sample_data <- mtcars[sample(nrow(mtcars), 1000, replace = TRUE), ]
ggplot(sample_data, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()





Start simple: Build plots incrementally
Check data first: Validate input data before plotting
Use reproducible examples: Create minimal examples that reproduce issues
Read error messages carefully: They often point to the exact problem
Check package versions: Ensure compatible versions of ggplot2 and extensions
Use debugging tools: Leverage R’s debugging functions and ggplot2’s debug options
Document fixes: Keep notes on solutions for future reference

title: Advanced Exporting Techniques
text:
This chapter covers advanced techniques for exporting plots, including programmatic generation, batch processing, custom devices, and integration with other tools.




library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)

# Create plots for each cylinder group
plots <- mtcars %>%
  split(.$cyl) %>%
  map(~ ggplot(.x, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + 
        geom_point() + 
        ggtitle(paste("Cylinders:", .x$cyl[1])))

# Save each plot
walk2(plots, names(plots), 
      ~ ggsave(filename = paste0("plot_cyl_", .x, ".png"), 
               plot = .y, 
               width = 6, height = 4))



# Generate timestamped filenames
timestamp <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")

ggsave(paste0("analysis_plot_", timestamp, ".pdf"), 
       plot = p, 
       width = 8, height = 6)






save_plot_multiple_formats <- function(plot, filename_base, 
                                     formats = c("png", "pdf", "svg")) {
  for (fmt in formats) {
    filename <- paste0(filename_base, ".", fmt)
    ggsave(filename, plot, width = 8, height = 6)
  }
}

# Usage
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
save_plot_multiple_formats(p, "mtcars_scatter")



datasets <- list(
  mtcars = mtcars,
  iris = iris,
  airquality = airquality
)

for (name in names(datasets)) {
  data <- datasets[[name]]
  # Create appropriate plot based on data
  if (name == "mtcars") {
    p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
  } else if (name == "iris") {
    p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, color = Species)) + 
      geom_point()
  }
  
  ggsave(paste0(name, "_plot.png"), p, width = 6, height = 4)
}






library(Cairo)

# High-quality PNG
CairoPNG("high_quality.png", width = 800, height = 600, 
         bg = "white", pointsize = 12)
plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
dev.off()

# PDF with embedded fonts
CairoPDF("embedded_fonts.pdf", width = 8, height = 6, 
         family = "Arial")
plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
dev.off()



# Create a custom device wrapper
save_high_res <- function(filename, plot_func, ...) {
  png(filename, width = 1200, height = 800, res = 150, ...)
  plot_func()
  dev.off()
}

# Usage
my_plot <- function() {
  plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg, 
       xlab = "Weight", ylab = "MPG",
       main = "High Resolution Plot")
}

save_high_res("high_res_plot.png", my_plot)






library(tikzDevice)

# Export as TikZ for LaTeX
tikz("plot.tex", width = 4, height = 3)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
dev.off()



# Export as HTML with plotly
library(plotly)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(ggplotly(p), "interactive_plot.html")






# Create publication-ready theme
publication_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12, family = "Times"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  publication_theme +
  labs(title = "Publication Quality Plot")

ggsave("publication_plot.pdf", p, 
       width = 6, height = 4, 
       device = cairo_pdf)



library(cowplot)

# Create individual plots
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) + geom_boxplot()
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = hp)) + geom_histogram()

# Combine into single figure
combined <- plot_grid(p1, p2, p3, 
                      labels = c("A", "B", "C"),
                      ncol = 2)

# Save combined figure
ggsave("combined_figure.pdf", combined, 
       width = 10, height = 8)






# For large datasets, use sampling or aggregation
large_data <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100000), y = rnorm(100000))

# Option 1: Sample data
sample_data <- large_data[sample(nrow(large_data), 10000), ]
ggplot(sample_data, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.1)
ggsave("sampled_plot.png")

# Option 2: Use density plots
ggplot(large_data, aes(x = x, y = y)) + 
  geom_density2d() +
  geom_point(data = sample_data, alpha = 0.1)
ggsave("density_plot.png")



# Clear graphics devices
graphics.off()

# Force garbage collection
gc()

# Monitor memory usage
library(pryr)
mem_used()






check_plot_quality <- function(filename) {
  # Check file exists
  if (!file.exists(filename)) {
    stop("File was not created")
  }
  
  # Check file size (basic quality indicator)
  size <- file.info(filename)$size
  if (size < 1000) {
    warning("File seems too small, may indicate error")
  }
  
  # For images, could check dimensions
  if (grepl("\\.png$", filename)) {
    img <- png::readPNG(filename)
    message("Image dimensions: ", dim(img)[1], "x", dim(img)[2])
  }
}

# Usage
ggsave("test_plot.png", ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point())
check_plot_quality("test_plot.png")





Automate repetitive tasks: Use functions and loops for batch processing
Standardize formats: Establish consistent dimensions and resolutions
Quality control: Implement checks for successful exports
Performance awareness: Optimize for large datasets
Version control: Track plot versions with timestamps or git
Documentation: Comment code for reproducible exports
Cross-platform compatibility: Test exports on target systems

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) + geom_boxplot()
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = hp)) + geom_histogram()

# Combine into single figure
combined <- plot_grid(p1, p2, p3, 
                      labels = c("A", "B", "C"),
                      ncol = 2)

# Save combined figure
ggsave("combined_figure.pdf", combined, 
       width = 10, height = 8)

large_data <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100000), y = rnorm(100000))

title: Exporting plots
text: Exporting plots from R can be done in several ways, depending on the desired output format and quality. Here are some common methods to export plots:

title: Exporting plots
text:
Using R’s Built-in Functions
R provides several built-in functions for exporting plots to different formats:

Raster Formats

png(), jpeg(), tiff(), bmp(): These functions save plots in raster formats. You can specify filename, dimensions, and resolution.

# PNG format (good for web)
png("plot.png", width = 800, height = 600, res = 100)
plot(x, y)
dev.off()

# High-resolution TIFF for publications
tiff("plot.tiff", width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(x, y)
dev.off()


Vector Formats

pdf(): Saves plots in PDF format, vector-based and scalable.
svg(): Saves plots in SVG format, ideal for web and scalable graphics.

# PDF for high-quality prints
pdf("plot.pdf", width = 8, height = 6)
plot(x, y)
dev.off()

# SVG for web use
svg("plot.svg", width = 8, height = 6)
plot(x, y)
dev.off()

title: Exporting plots
text:
Exporting ggplot2 Plots
For ggplot2 plots, the ggsave() function is the most convenient way to export:
library(ggplot2)

# Create a plot
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point()

# Save in different formats
ggsave("plot.png", p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)
ggsave("plot.pdf", p, width = 8, height = 6)
ggsave("plot.svg", p, width = 8, height = 6)

Controlling Output Quality

Resolution (DPI): Higher DPI for print quality (300+), lower for web (72-150)
Dimensions: Specify in inches or pixels
Aspect Ratio: Maintain proportions for consistency

# High-resolution for publications
ggsave("publication_plot.tiff", p, 
       width = 6, height = 4, 
       dpi = 300, 
       device = "tiff")

# Web-optimized PNG
ggsave("web_plot.png", p, 
       width = 800, height = 600, 
       dpi = 100, 
       units = "px")

Exporting Multiple Plots
# Save multiple plots to PDF
pdf("multiple_plots.pdf")
plot1 <- ggplot(data1, aes(x, y)) + geom_point()
print(plot1)
plot2 <- ggplot(data2, aes(x, y)) + geom_line()

Using Cairo for Better Quality
The Cairo graphics library can provide better quality for some formats:
install.packages("Cairo")
library(Cairo)

CairoPNG("high_quality.png", width = 800, height = 600)
plot(x, y)
dev.off()


Exporting to Clipboard
For quick sharing:
# Windows
savePlot("clipboard", type = "wmf")

# Or for ggplot2
ggsave("clipboard", p, device = "png")

title: Exporting plots
text:
Best Practices

Choose the right format: PDF/SVG for vector graphics, PNG/TIFF for raster
Set appropriate resolution: 300 DPI for print, 72-150 for screen
Consider file size: Vector formats scale better but may be larger
Test outputs: Always check exported files in target applications
Use consistent dimensions: Maintain aspect ratios across exports

title: Exporting plots
text:
Common Issues and Solutions

Plot not saving: Ensure dev.off() is called after plotting
Low quality: Increase DPI or use vector formats
Wrong dimensions: Specify units explicitly (inches, cm, pixels)
Colors not matching: Check color profiles and device settings
